main_text.p: 'Αξίδω, inter alia, peto, postulo, to afke. Litera ξ sæpe mutatur in σ. ut σκιῳ, pro ξίῳ ; σκιφία, pro ξιφίας ; ἀξίνη, afcia : ut alia omittam ex linguâ Etrusca, (sive Italicâ ;) & Hispanicâ, doctissimo Caninio notata. Germani ochs, quod Angli ofe ; Belgæ, os.

*Αρνυμαι. Deest Latinis verbum, quo exprimant. Nam capio, recipio, confequor ; & similia, sunt nimis generalia. Angli optime, to earne : ut in vulgaribus illis exemplis, ἀρνυς μίσθον, to earne wages : ἀρνυς βίλον ἐκ χειρῶν, to earne his living with his hands. Ab eádem autem origine est earnest ; pro, serius, vel studiosus. Cætera enim pleraque quasi per jocum & perfunctorie : at ubi lucri res agitur, (talis præcipuè ex quo vita pendet, qui Græcis ideò βίω) tum serii, & si unquam, animis intenti plerique sumus. Sed & verbum ἀρνυς, pro studiosè aliquid prosequi, olim sine dubio vulgare, cujus apud Homerum vestigia significationis, in istis, quæ doctissimus Stephanus ex

page.notes: Marginal marks at right (handwritten/pencil strokes and asterisks) are not transcribed. Greek and some English words in the text are in black letter/italic as printed; the English glosses ("to earne", "wages", "his living", etc.) are set in English type. Some Greek accents are uncertain and may be imperfect. The final line "ex" appears at the foot of the column and was transcribed as a closing fragment.
